fixture_note: Scenario 2: evaluate an enterprise agent-governance proposal on incomplete evidence. Expected outcome REVIEW with NO_RECOMMENDATION because no option clears the GOVERNANCE_EVALUATION evidence threshold of three distinct records across two independent sources. Exercises the maximum route depth of nine and activates the abductive operator.

intake.problem_statement: An enterprise buyer proposes adopting an agent-governance control layer across four business units, and we must evaluate whether the proposal as written is adoptable.
constraints: no access to the buyer's incident data
evaluation must complete before the next steering review

observations.statement: The proposal claims a 40 percent reduction in unapproved agent actions but cites no measurement method.
Two of the four business units are absent from the proposal's rollout schedule without explanation.

options.label: Adopt the proposal as written
options.mechanism: Accept the stated control set, rollout schedule, and success measures without modification and begin the first business unit next quarter.
options.tradeoff: Accepts the proposal's unmeasured effectiveness claim as the baseline for later evaluation.

options.label: Adopt conditionally after an evidence round
options.mechanism: Require measured baseline data and a stated rollout rationale for the two absent units before any adoption decision is taken.
options.tradeoff: Delays the decision by at least one steering cycle.

evidence_register.claim_supported: The proposed control set is documented.
A 40 percent reduction in unapproved actions is asserted.
The rollout schedule covers two of four business units.
A conditional adoption path is already defined in the control standard.

assumptions: The proposal document supplied is the complete and current version.

primitives.statement: The proposal defines a control set.
The effectiveness figure has no stated measurement method.
Whether the absent business units were excluded deliberately is unknown.
A conditional adoption route exists in the standard.

claims.statement: The proposal's central effectiveness claim rests on an unstated measurement method, so adoption as written would import an unverifiable baseline.
A conditional adoption route is already permitted by the internal standard.

assumptions: Business units share one identity provider.

relations.mechanism: credential scope changes are tracked as changes
change records feed the audit trail
audit findings constrain what the runtime may do

feedback_loops.effect: Audit findings constrain runtime permissions, so a partial rollout leaves two business units outside the balancing loop entirely.

claims.statement: A rollout covering half the business units leaves the remaining units outside the balancing loop, which weakens the control rather than partially applying it.

assumptions: Rejecting the proposal outright is out of scope for this evaluation.

options.label: Adopt the proposal as written
options.mechanism: Accept the stated control set, rollout schedule, and success measures without modification and begin the first business unit next quarter.
options.tradeoff: Accepts the proposal's unmeasured effectiveness claim as the baseline for later evaluation.

options.label: Adopt conditionally after an evidence round
options.mechanism: Require measured baseline data and a stated rollout rationale for the two absent units before any adoption decision is taken.
options.tradeoff: Delays the decision by at least one steering cycle.

options.label: Run a bounded pilot in one business unit
options.mechanism: Instrument a single unit for one quarter to generate the missing baseline internally instead of requesting it.
options.tradeoff: Spends internal capacity to produce evidence the proposer should have supplied.

claims.statement: Three routes exist: accept the stated terms, require evidence first, or generate the missing evidence internally.

assumptions: The proposer had access to their own incident data when writing the proposal.

hypotheses.statement: The two absent business units were omitted because their agent estate is not yet inventoried, and the effectiveness figure comes from a pilot in the two included units only.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Request the inventory status of the two absent units; if inventories exist, this hypothesis is false.

hypotheses.statement: The figure is a vendor benchmark rather than a buyer measurement, and the absent units are covered by a separate programme.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Ask for the source system of the 40 percent figure; a vendor document rather than buyer telemetry confirms this hypothesis.

claims.statement: The leading explanation for both anomalies is a partial inventory, which is testable by requesting inventory status and is not yet established.

defects.statement: The 40 percent effectiveness figure has no measurement method, population, or period attached.
defects.remediation: Require the measurement method, sample population, and observation window before the figure is used in any decision.

defects.statement: The rollout covers only the units most likely to succeed, so a favourable result would not generalise.
defects.remediation: Require the selection rationale for the included units.

defects.statement: Three of four evidence records originate from a single buyer-supplied source, so the evidence base is not independent.
defects.remediation: Obtain at least one measurement from a source the proposer does not control.

claims.statement: The evidence base is dominated by one interested source and cannot support an adoption decision at this task class.

failure_modes.statement: Adoption proceeds, the unmeasured baseline turns out to be wrong, and the control set is credited with an improvement it did not cause.
failure_modes.precondition: The 40 percent figure is never independently reproduced after adoption.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Post-adoption incident rate does not move despite reported control coverage.

failure_modes.statement: The two absent units remain outside the control perimeter and become the route around the governance layer.
failure_modes.precondition: No rollout rationale is supplied for the absent units and they are never scheduled.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Agent activity in the absent units grows relative to the covered units.

failure_modes.statement: The evidence round is requested, the buyer declines, and the evaluation stalls without a decision.
failure_modes.precondition: The buyer treats the evidence request as a rejection.
failure_modes.detection_signal: No response to the evidence request within one steering cycle.

claims.statement: The dominant failure mode of adopting as written is irreversible attribution of an unearned improvement to the control set.

assumptions: The steering review treats this evaluation as precedent for later proposals.

effects.statement: Accepting an unmeasured effectiveness claim once establishes that vendor-asserted figures are adoptable, which lowers the evidence bar for every later proposal.
effects.follows_from: The proposal is adopted as written.

effects.statement: Requiring measured evidence once sets the expectation that proposers supply baselines, which shifts evidence cost to the party that can produce it cheapest.

claims.statement: Because this evaluation is precedent-setting, the downstream cost of accepting an unmeasured claim exceeds the immediate cost of delay.
